sub: Call it before you know it. Wrong is where it gets good.

1.name: Cold Read
q: Guess their coffee order out loud — size, milk, all of it.~Wrong? Don't defend it. Just say what made you picture that.
On three, both say how late the other one usually runs. Three, two, one.~Whoever's further off goes first on the next card.
Before you guess, rate how well you know their taste in music, one to ten. Say the number.~Then guess their karaoke song. Said seven or higher and missed? They pick your next answer for you.
Guess their childhood bedroom — but guess it badly on purpose. The worst version you can picture.~They tell you which part you accidentally got right.
Guess the last thing they searched. When they tell you the truth, argue yours was more interesting.~They decide who wins. No appeal.
They're going to tell you their worst habit — and they might lie about it. You get one call: true or lie.~Call it out loud before they can react.
Look away. They tell the room what they were doing an hour before this.~Now turn back and repeat it to them. Every detail you dropped, they get to ask you something.
Guess their most-used emoji. Commit before they check.
Bet now on something you'll find out later tonight: do they skip a card before the deck's done? Yes or no.~Say it out loud. It gets settled at the end.
Both point at whoever's more likely to be late. Three, two, one — point.~Pointed at each other? You're both right, and you both explain.
Guess what's in their bag or pockets. Three things.~Every miss, they ask you one question you have to answer straight.
Guess whether they make the bed. Say it like you're certain.
Guess their 2am order, all of it.~Wrong? Yours is next, and you don't get to make it sound better than it is.
Say what you think their friends call them behind their back — the affectionate version.~They tell you the real one, if there is one.
On three, both say which of you is the bigger overthinker.~Same answer? That's your answer. Different? Both defend it.
Guess the app they'd be embarrassed to have open right now. One shot.
Guess what they notice first about people. Say it, then find out.
They answer this one, and they may or may not be lying: what's your most irrational fear?~One call. True or lie. Say it before you think too hard.
Guess how they'd spend a completely free Saturday — no plans, no obligations.~Wrong? Describe yours, and it has to be the real one, not the impressive one.
Rate how well you know their family, one to ten. Say it first.~Now guess which parent they're more like. Overconfident and wrong is the worst outcome here.
Guess the compliment they get most often.
Look away and let them describe you to the room in one sentence.~Turn back. Guess what they said, word for word.
Guess their opinion of the food here before they give it. Be specific about how harsh.
Guess what they do first when they get home. Commit out loud.
Say the worst possible guess for their dream job. Deliberately terrible.~They tell you what's weirdly right about it.
Guess their biggest waste of money — then argue yours was a better decision than theirs.~They judge. Winner picks who answers first next time.
On three, both guess how long you'll both keep playing tonight. Numbers out loud.~Closest one picks the last card of the night.
Guess how they take criticism: badly, quietly, or too well.~Then give them some and watch which one it is.
Guess whether they've properly Googled you. Yes or no, out loud, no hedging.
Guess the thing they're weirdly good at that hasn't come up yet.
They're going to tell you their proudest moment from school, and one detail will be invented.~Your job is to name the invented detail.
Guess what they'd grab if the place caught fire and they had ten seconds.
Guess how long they take to reply to a text they don't want to answer.~Then they check their phone and prove you wrong.
Say what you think they were most nervous about tonight. Guess first, ask second.
Guess their comfort show — the one they've rewatched too many times.~Wrong? They get to judge your last five watched.
Bet now, settled later: will they save a card tonight? Yes or no. Say it out loud.
Guess what they think this deck is going to be like by the end of it.
Guess whether they were the funny one, the smart one, or the quiet one at school.~Wrong? They tell you which one you obviously were.
On three, both say a number: how many drinks in before either of you gets properly honest.~Compare. The lower number explains themselves.

2.name: Warmer
q: Guess what they're proudest of.~Whether you're right or wrong, the interesting part is the same: say why you guessed that.
On three, both say who's more afraid of being boring. Three, two, one — point.~Whoever gets pointed at answers why.
Rate how well you actually know them, one to ten. Say the number before you guess anything.~Now guess what they're hardest on themselves about. That number is the thing on the line.
Guess the thing they've quietly given up on. Say it carefully.~Being wrong here is a good outcome. Ask what it really is.
Guess what they wanted to be at ten years old. When they tell you, argue your version suits them better.~They decide whether you've got a point.
They'll answer this, and they might be protecting themselves: what's the best decision you've ever made?~One call — is that the real answer, or the safe one?
Look away. They tell the room what they're avoiding right now in their life.~Turn back and guess what they said. Then say yours.
Guess what their friends rely on them for.
Say the worst possible guess for what makes them feel like themselves. Deliberately, comically wrong.~Then they tell you the real one, and it lands harder for the contrast.
Guess what they need more of right now — rest, money, people, or something to work toward.~Wrong? Say what you saw that made you guess it anyway.
On three, both say whether you think the other is happier now than five years ago.~Then you each answer it for yourselves. Compare what you got wrong.
Guess the compliment that would actually land with them, versus the one they hear constantly.~Then give them the one you guessed and see if it worked.
Guess what they're most afraid people think about them.
Bet now, settled at the end of the deck: will they tell you something tonight they've never told anyone?~Yes or no. Say it out loud and remember it.
Guess what they'd fix about themselves if it were free and instant.~Wrong? Tell them what you'd have picked for them instead — carefully.
Guess who in their life they're most worried about right now.
They'll tell you what their last relationship taught them. One part will be the version they've rehearsed.~Name which part.
Guess the age they felt most confident. Say a number out loud.~More than five years off? They explain what actually happened at the age you guessed.
Guess what they say yes to when they mean no.
Look away. They tell the room the thing they'd never let anyone film.~You don't get to hear the details. Just guess the category.
Guess what stops them from asking for help.~Wrong? Tell them what stops you. That one you have to get right.
On three, both name who'd fall apart first if things went badly.~Different answers means one of you is being polite. Sort it out.
Guess who they'd call at 3am — and whether that person knows it.
Guess what they miss that they don't talk about.~Say why you thought that before they answer.
Guess what they're better at than they give themselves credit for. Then they argue with you, and you have to hold your ground.
Guess what they've never told their family. Not the thing itself — just what kind of thing it is.
Rate your confidence, one to ten, then guess: do they think they're easy to love?~High confidence and wrong is the answer to a different question entirely.
Guess what they'd do differently if nobody would ever find out.
Say the worst guess you can for what they're waiting for. Then the real one.~They tell you which was closer. Sometimes it's the joke.
Guess the thing they'd want said about them at the end.~This one's worth the silence after. Don't fill it.
They'll tell you the loneliest they've ever been. They may soften it.~One call: is that the softened version?
Guess how they'd describe their relationship with their own ambition.
On three, both say which of you is more likely to settle for less than you want.~Both explain. Neither of you gets to just point.
Guess what the last few years have cost them.~Wrong? Ask properly. This is the one to get wrong and then listen.
Guess what they think about on the way home from a night out.
Look away. They say out loud the thing they'd change about how they were raised.~Turn back and guess it. Close counts here.
Guess what they'd never do again, no matter what.
Guess the thing they'd be doing if they'd been slightly braver at twenty-two.

3.name: Dead On
q: Guess what they've been thinking about you for the last ten minutes.~Then they tell you. No softening it.
On three, both rate tonight out of ten. Numbers out loud, at the same time.~Different? The lower one explains first.
Guess the thing they've almost said tonight and didn't.~Wrong? Ask what it actually was. Then wait, and don't fill the silence.
They'll tell you their honest first impression of you. They might spare you.~One call: real, or spared?
Rate how well you think you've read them tonight, one to ten. Say it before they respond.~Then they give you their number for the same thing. Live with the gap.
Guess what they think you're hiding.~Say why you think they think that. That part's more revealing than the guess.
Look away. They tell the room the one question they've been hoping you'd ask.~Turn back, guess it, then ask it properly whether you got it or not.
Rate, one to ten, how sure you are they'll want to do this again. Say the number out loud, then find out.~Anything above a seven that turns out wrong is worth sitting with.
Guess what they were thinking in the first ten seconds of meeting you.~Unedited version only. That's the deal.
Guess the moment tonight they actually relaxed. Name it specifically.
Guess what they'd say is the best thing about you — then argue for a different one.~They decide which is more true. You have to accept the verdict.
Settle the bet you made at the start: were you right about them? Both of you, out loud.~Whoever read the other better gets one free question, right now.
On three, both say what the other one isn't saying right now. Same moment.~Whoever landed closer gets to ask about theirs.
On three, both say what you want to happen after this. Same moment, no hedging.~Say it before you hear theirs. That's the whole point.
Guess the thing about you they find hardest to read.~Wrong? They tell you the real one, and it's usually worse.
Guess what they'd want you to understand about them that you probably don't yet.
Say the worst possible guess for what they think of you. The most unflattering thing you can.~Then they tell you how far off it was. Hopefully quite far.
Guess what they'll remember about tonight in a month. One thing.
Guess whether they think you've been fully honest tonight.~They answer properly. You don't get to defend yourself until after.
Look away. They say out loud what they'd change about you if they could.~Turn back. Guess it before they repeat it.
They'll tell you what they've decided about you tonight — and they might hand you the generous version.~One call: generous, or true?
Guess what would make them trust you.~Wrong? Ask. Then decide out loud whether you can do it.
They'll say the truest thing they've said all night. It might not be the one you'd pick.~Guess which card it was first.
On three, both say whether you feel more known than when you started.~Then whoever said less has to say what's missing.
Look away. They say the thing they'd tell you if they knew you'd forget it by morning.~Turn back and guess it. You don't get to ask them to repeat it.
Guess what scared them most about tonight going well.
Rate, one to ten, how much you think they've held back. Say your number.~Then they say theirs. If yours was lower, you weren't paying attention.
Guess the thing you've done tonight that landed best.~Then the thing that landed worst. They confirm both.
Guess what they think this is. Say the word out loud before they do.
Guess what they'll leave out when they tell someone about tonight. When they answer, argue they should leave in the opposite thing.~They decide who's right about their own story.
Look away. They tell the room what they need to hear right now.~Turn back, guess it, and then say it to them properly.
On three, both name the one thing you'd redo from this conversation.~Named the same moment? Then talk about it properly.
On three, both point at whoever's been braver tonight.~Pointed at yourself? Justify it.
Guess what they think you want to hear — then tell them whether they're right.
Guess what you've got wrong about them so far.~They correct exactly one thing. Just one. Believe it.
Guess whether they'd tell you if this wasn't working. Yes or no, out loud, before they answer.

wild: Both write a one-word guess for how tonight ends. Don't show each other. On three, reveal.
Guess their answer to the next card before it's drawn. Say it out loud, then draw.
Both point at whoever's been more honest so far. Three, two, one.~Different directions? Both explain.
Guess what they'd say your best feature is. Say your guess, then they say the real one.
Both say a number on three: how well you know each other, out of ten.~If they don't match, the higher one justifies it.
Predict whether they're about to skip this card. Say it before they decide.
Both guess the other's mood in one word. On three. No adjusting after you hear theirs.
Say what you think they're about to say — then let them say it. Do it for the next card too.
Guess their answer, but say it in their voice. They grade the impression and the accuracy separately.
Name the topic they'll dodge tonight. Say it out loud now — see if you're right by the end.
Both guess who'll bring up tonight first tomorrow. Point on three.
Deliberately guess wrong on the next card. See if being wrong on purpose is any easier.
Bet the next card is a question they can't answer honestly. If you're right, they owe you one that they can.
Guess which card so far has been their favourite. One shot.
Trade phones for ten seconds. Guess what they'll look at first.
Both close your eyes. On three, say the first true thing about the other that comes to mind.
Guess how many cards until one of you gets uncomfortable. Say a number.
You get one free guess about them tonight, no consequences. Use it now or lose it.
final: Last guess of the night, and it's the only one that counts. Say out loud what you think tonight meant to them.
Now they tell you how close you got. No editing it to be kind.
Whatever the gap was between those two answers — that's the thing worth talking about on the way home.
